text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

Robusta futures in London finished higher on late covering ahead of the three-day weekend. New York's reversal from Thursday's rally had no real impact in London as the market did not react when New York moved up. May closed $15 higher at $1,590 per tonne, while July added $10 to close at $1,670 per tonne.

Arabica futures in New York pulled back in their first attempt to correct the extremely overbought situation. However, it remains to be seen whether we have seen the top of the market. This is not likely to be the case as the tightness is not expected to be alleviated and exports are likely to come down in the months ahead which will put further pressure on supplies. This will be especially the case if the Colombian crop should be short of even the most recent projections. May closed 5.20 cents/lb easier at 247.55 cents/lb, while July gave up 6.75 cents/lb to close at 216.15 cents/lb.

INTERNATIONAL - German coffee trade house Bernard Rothfos said Brazil's 1997/98 coffee harvest appears likely to total between 24 and 25.5 mn 60-kg bags, down 15-20 per cent from 1996/97. In its latest quarterly digest report, Rothfos said the 1996/97 crop, which is now drawing to a close, has finished higher than expected. It now estimates output will be 30 mn bags, up from its last estimate of 27 mn bags in January.

With exports still running strong most sources agreed to a larger crop than originally expected, Rothfos said. Rothfos estimated that stocks of coffee in consumer countries will total 7.66 mn 60-kg bags by the end of 1996/97 (October/September) down 612,000 bags from the start of the season. Rothfos said stocks in producing countries will total 22.8 mn bags, down 1.4 mn bags from the start of the season.

It added there will be a draw down of 2 mn bags from stocks of coffee at origin in the American milds category as Colombia, Costa Rica and El Salvador all reduce stocks 'in order to achieve export goals.' The stock estimates are based on a number of factors. Rothfos estimates that 1996/97 world production will total 97 mn bags; consumption within origin countries will be 24.0 mn bags; consumption in consuming countries will total 75 mn bags; and producers will export 73 mn bags during the season.

The report said consumer stock levels decreased up until the end of last year but are likely to rise between January and May. It sees the decrease resuming after May to take stocks down to 7.66 mn bags, equivalent to 5.3 weeks of coverage, which it said is 'a level dangerously below the excepted minimum required by the industry.' According to Rothfos, global stocks at the end of 1996/97 will represent 41 per cent of global disappearance, compared with 59 per cent at the end of 1993/94.

More significant is that stocks of mild coffee now represent 29 per cent of mild coffee disappearance, down from 52 per cent three seasons ago. Robusta stocks are seen at 28 per cent, compared with 24 per cent in 1993/94, while unwashed arabica stocks are estimated at 87 per cent, down from 126 per cent.

UNITED STATES - Coffee roastings totalled approximately 315,000 60-kg bags during the week ended April 26 up from 295,000 bags the previous week and compared with 325,000 bags in the corresponding week one year ago, Complete Coffee Coverage said. Cumulative roastings totalled 5.710 mn 60-kg bags versus 5.580 mn bags in the same year ago period.

UNITED KINGDOM - The UK imported 291,036 bags of coffee in January 1997, 14 per cent more than was imported the same month the previous year. Total imports in calendar year 1996 rose by nearly 12 per cent to 3.114 mn bags. Main suppliers of green coffee in January 1997 were Uganda (25,600 vs 5,500 bags), Colombia (27,100 vs 26,500 bags), Indonesia (44,000 vs 19,300 bags) and Vietnam (31,500 vs 38,500 bags). The country exported 42,700 bags of coffee in January 1997, nearly 13 per cent less than was exported the same month the previous year. Total exports in calendar year 1996 rose by 1 per cent to 542,600 bags.
